text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dutch financial group ING is keen to take full control of U.S. merchant bank Dillon Read in which it now holds a 25 percent stake. (p1)
- Lower oil price leads to lower first-quarter earnings for Royal Dutch/Shell. (p1)
- Building firms Volker Stevin and Kondor Wessels plan to triple annual revenues in Germany to around one billion guilders on completion of their planned merger. (p1)
- Dutch organisation Stichting Performance is to advise Russian companies Lada and Gazprom about setting up pension funds for their employees. (p1)
- Pilots at airline KLM seek shares, share options or seat on company's supervisory board in exchange for commitment sought by management to moderate pay demands. (p2)
- City of Maastricht disappointed that Noordwijk, not Maastricht, will be site for extra European Union summit meeting this month, if an extra summit is indeed called. (p1)
- EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek says EU must not be too hasty in admitting new members from East Europe because their economies are not yet ready for free competition. (p27)
